query: Test whether our assistant chooses the right inventory capability among similar tool names. Include distractors, invalid units, absent evidence, and tasks where no call should be made.

Benchmark the current and revised tool catalogues on identical tasks. Separate discovery, selection, arguments, response interpretation, redundant calls, and recovery rather than only checking final answers.
Evaluate a search-read-update chain where the model must use a returned ID and current version. Allow alternative safe sequences, but reject fabricated identifiers and unauthorized committed effects.
Our model claims it changed a ticket without a receipt. Build tool-use cases that join calls to final state and distinguish a correct final sentence from an actually completed mutation.

Create usability tests for tools that return empty, truncated, malformed, and paginated results. Measure whether the model interprets each state and obtains missing evidence within a bounded call budget.
We renamed two agent tools and selection errors increased. Design matched cases with plausible distractors and repeated runs, then identify whether failures begin in discovery or semantic choice.
Evaluate model behavior when a mutation times out after committing. Use an idempotent fake and inspect whether it reconciles the outcome instead of blindly repeating or minting a new operation.
Test an assistant tool surface under rate limits, stale versions, authorization denials, cancellation, and exhausted budgets. Score failure recovery separately from server contract correctness.
Users ask ambiguous bulk-update requests and the model picks an overly broad tool. Create substantial cases for clarification, safe abstention, argument scope, and forbidden effects in sandbox state.

Compare whether removing unused tools improves an LLM workflow. Freeze fixtures, prompts, permissions, and initial state; report selection errors and valid chain dependencies without demanding one transcript.

Redesign ambiguous lookup and mutation tools for our assistant. Produce names, descriptions, schemas, actionable errors, idempotency rules, and success and denial exchanges before any usability measurement.

Build a representative benchmark for whole-agent research answers, covering factual accuracy, source support, completeness, safe abstention, and severity-weighted release slices. Tool usability is already acceptable.
Write unit and adapter tests for the server pagination and error mapping. Call the functions directly with fixed inputs; this request has no model selecting or interpreting capabilities.

Implement a new MCP integration from official SDK examples, including transport setup, registration, structured response handling, build verification, and Inspector smoke checks for the provided contract.

Specify crash recovery for an agent operation ledger when an external effect is committed but no receipt is stored. Define reconciliation, compensation, resume authorization, and terminal partial statuses.

Threat-model whether malicious tool metadata can induce credential exfiltration. Map attacker-controlled text to proposed actions and verify destination policies and scoped identities prevent forbidden effects.
Create a typed schema for model-produced plans, refusals, and missing evidence. Test semantic consistency and unknown versions; the output is advisory data and invokes no external capability.

Rewrite the production instructions that tell our assistant when to stop. Remove conflicting examples and define evidence requirements against the existing tool catalogue and established regression suite.
Compare model routing and cache policies for an assistant whose task quality is already scored. Include retries and fallback charges in cost per success and keep p95 completion within budget.
Add tracing around discovery, tool attempts, policy denial, and final receipt linkage. We need run reconstruction and safe event retention, not new usability cases or quality scores.
